title: Functorial bounded-above flat replacement
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme and $\Lambda$ a commutative ring, with $\Lambda_T$ its constant sheaf of rings on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Use cochain complexes and quasi-isomorphisms as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and flat module sheaves as in [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. There is a construction which assigns to every bounded-above complex
$\mathcal F^\bullet$ of $\Lambda_T$-module sheaves together with an
integer $N$ such that $\mathcal F^i=0$ for $i>N$ a bounded-above
complex $\Phi(\mathcal F)^\bullet$ of flat $\Lambda_T$-module
sheaves with $\Phi(\mathcal F)^i=0$ for $i>N$ and a termwise
surjective quasi-isomorphism
$\Phi(\mathcal F)^\bullet\to\mathcal F^\bullet$; the construction is
functorial, in the sense that a map
$\mathcal F^\bullet\to\mathcal G^\bullet$ between complexes which both
vanish above $N$ induces a map
$\Phi(\mathcal F)^\bullet\to\Phi(\mathcal G)^\bullet$ compatible with
the two quasi-isomorphisms. In particular every bounded-above complex
of $\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$-module sheaves on $T_{\Et}$ is quasi-isomorphic to a
bounded-above complex of flat sheaves. Here the last assertion holds for every integer $n$.

proof.text: Let R be the constant commutative ring sheaf on the small etale site and O its underlying ring sheaf. Work directly with O-modules, retaining the site object universe u+1, site morphism universe u, and coefficient/module universe u+1. Forget a module sheaf to an O-presheaf, take the sectionwise free module on its underlying presheaf of sets, and sheafify. Evaluation sends the basis vector indexed by a section to that section; it is natural and sectionwise surjective. The free functor and sheafification are actual constructions. Their counits define a natural augmentation pi:T -> Id, epic because sheafification preserves epimorphisms and its counit on sheaves is an isomorphism.

source.place: 03EW (lemma-module-quotient-flat), sheafification route in the last sentence of the proof

proof.text: Each section module of the free presheaf is free, hence flat. Its sectionwise tensor functor preserves finite limits, and evaluation jointly reflects limits. For module sheafification a and its right adjoint V, the monoidal sheafification comparison and invertible counit give tensorRight(a(F)) isomorphic to V followed by tensorRight(F) followed by a. The latter preserves finite limits, since V is a right adjoint and module sheafification is left exact. Thus the sheaf cover is flat. Tensor preserves finite colimits by the independent-universe tensor-colimit theorem and symmetry. The same theorem makes tensor additive; zero objects are flat because tensoring a zero object is the zero functor. The proof constructs the tensor comparison explicitly from Mathlib functor unitors, associators, the sheafification counit and Functor.Monoidal.commTensorRight, so it needs no equal-universe flat-sheafification wrapper.

Apply the existing generic functorial cycle-pullback construction with S the categorical flat objects, the constructed free-sheaf cover T and its epic augmentation pi. It supplies Q, epsilon, flat terms, zero terms above N, and lifts after epic refinements for every compatible pair consisting of a next-degree source cycle x and current-degree target map y with epsilon(x)=d(y). This retains the repaired cycle pullback, rather than the erroneous full-next-term pullback of the imported blueprint.

Prove epsilon termwise epic using the generalized-element refinement criterion. Given y:B -> F^i, first lift the compatible pair (0,d(y)) in degree i+1 after an epic p1:B1 -> B, obtaining a cycle x1 in QF^(i+1). Then lift (x1,p1 followed by y) in degree i after an epic p2:B2 -> B1. Its augmentation equals p2 followed by p1 followed by y. The composite of the two epimorphisms is epic.

source.place: 05T7 (1), verification of termwise surjectivity using the cycle induction hypothesis

proof.text: Prove epsilon a quasi-isomorphism using Mathlib HomologicalComplex.mono_homologyMap_iff_up_to_refinements and epi_homologyMap_iff_up_to_refinements. For monicity in degree i, a source cycle x whose augmentation is the boundary d(y) is a compatible pair in degree i-1; its lift z satisfies d(z)=p followed by x. For epimorphy, a target cycle y lifts through (0,y) in degree i; the lift is a cycle and maps to p followed by y, with boundary correction zero. Thus each homology map is both mono and epi, hence an isomorphism in the abelian category.

source.place: 05T7 (1), injectivity and surjectivity on cohomology by compatible-pair lifts

proof.text: Precompose Q and epsilon with the full-subcategory inclusion sending IsStrictlyLE N to explicit zero terms above N via CochainComplex.isStrictlyLE_iff. Its objects and maps are unchanged, so the resulting augmentation is natural. Convert the output bound with the same equivalence and categorical flatness using siteSheafTensorRightIso. For the final assertion set Lambda=ULift(ZMod(n.natAbs)), evaluate the functor and augmentation at the supplied bounded complex, and retain the bound, flatness and quasi-isomorphism. Every integer n, including zero and negative n, is covered.

proof_origin.place: 05T7 (1), using the already declared functorial cycle-pullback construction and a constructed free-presheaf/sheafification cover over the given ring sheaf (03EW, 03ET, 03EP); Lean refinement criteria prove termwise epimorphy and quasi-isomorphy.

Introduced T and Lambda explicitly and expanded the coefficient macro; no mathematical hypothesis added.

lean.statement: theorem exists_functorial_bounded_flat_replacement (T : Scheme.{u}) (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ] (N : ℤ) : ∃ (Φ : ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (fun K : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u + 1} ((sheafCompose T.smallEtaleTopology (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u + 1} RingCat.{u + 1})).obj ((constantSheaf T.smallEtaleTopology CommRingCat.{u + 1}).obj (CommRingCat.of Λ)))) ℤ ↦ K.IsStrictlyLE N) ⥤ CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u + 1} ((sheafCompose T.smallEtaleTopology (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u + 1} RingCat.{u + 1})).obj ((constantSheaf T.smallEtaleTopology CommRingCat.{u + 1}).obj (CommRingCat.of Λ)))) ℤ) (ε : Φ ⟶ ObjectProperty.ι _), ∀ F, (Φ.obj F).IsStrictlyLE N ∧ (∀ i : ℤ, SheafOfModules.IsFlatOnSite (J := T.smallEtaleTopology) (R := (constantSheaf T.smallEtaleTopology CommRingCat.{u + 1}).obj (CommRingCat.of Λ)) ((Φ.obj F).X i)) ∧ QuasiIso (ε.app F) ∧ (∀ i : ℤ, Epi ((ε.app F).f i))
